question:
A 46-year-old female patient seeks medical attention for fatigue and generalized dull headaches that
have persisted for one month and are worsening. She reports diplopia, progressive loss of peripheral
vision, and difficulty with weight management despite diet and exercise. She has gained 9 kg in the
past month and has a BMI of 30.4 kg/m². She has no significant past medical or surgical history. Her
vital signs show: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 60/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and blood pressure
121/80 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals bilateral papilledema, bitemporal hemianopsia,
diminished deep tendon reflexes, and pedal edema. Brain CT demonstrates suprasellar calcifications.
Laboratory findings are: | Na+ | 140 mEq/L | | --- | --- | | K+ | 3.8 mEq/L | | Serum calcium | 9.5 mg/dL | |
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) | 0.05 U/mL | | Free T4 | 0.2 ng/mL | Which diagnosis best explains
these findings? Answer Choices: (A) Rathke's cleft cyst (B) Germinoma (C) Pituitary adenoma (D)
Empty sella syndrome (E) Lymphocytic hypophysitis (F) Craniopharyngioma (G) Metastatic tumor (H)
Arachnoid cyst (I) Meningioma (J) Primary hypothyroidism
 A. Metastatic tumor
B. Pituitary adenoma
C. Meningioma
D. Rathke's cleft cyst
E. Primary hypothyroidism
F. Lymphocytic hypophysitis
G. Empty sella syndrome
H. Germinoma
I. Craniopharyngioma
J. Arachnoid cyst
